predecessors.note: Rewa is the first state the Vindhya Pradesh page names among the '36 princely states' merged on 12 March 1948; its maharaja Martand Singh was the first Rajpramukh.

predecessors.note: The page's infobox 'Preceded by: Central India Agency'; the other 35 princely states have no dossier and the Central India Agency has none either, so this land is nobody's before 1948 in the compiled map.

land.text: Vindhya Pradesh, 61,131.5 km2: the eastern princely states of the former Central India Agency, the Baghelkhand division (Rewa, Nagod, Maihar, and the rest of the plateau) and the Bundelkhand division (Panna, Chhatarpur, Orchha, Datia and the rest)

successors.note: 'The state was dissolved on 31 October 1956 and merged with Madhya Pradesh' (the page also says 'merged into Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 1956'). Charkhari and Samthar had been transferred out on 25 January 1950 (to Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Bharat). The madhya-bharat dossier names madhya-pradesh as its successor too; no dossier for it exists. [orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026: madhya-pradesh has no dossier; the land stays with the Republic of India]

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria shape; the p1940-p1949 window reports Rewa and the Baghelkhand states nobody's from 1948, and Cliopatria's India shape does not cover them). Infobox area 61,131.5 km2 against 68,789 km2 (272 cells) for this region: ratio 1.13, within a factor of two. The region is the researcher's: the Rewa State outline of the rewa-state dossier (Baghelkhand plateau) joined to the Madhya Pradesh part of Bundelkhand within 140 km of Panna and 45 km of Datia (coordinate discs, no gazetteer place for these towns). The page lists 36 states and eight districts in two divisions but no district names; Charkhari and Samthar (Uttar Pradesh, transferred in 1950) are not drawn. The Baghelkhand page gives the region 42,179 km2 (Singrauli, Rewa, Satna, Shahdol, Sidhi, Anuppur, Umaria, Maihar, Mauganj).

region.text: Vindhya Pradesh, 61,131.5 km2: the eastern princely states of the former Central India Agency, the Baghelkhand division (Rewa, Nagod, Maihar, and the rest of the plateau) and the Bundelkhand division (Panna, Chhatarpur, Orchha, Datia and the rest)

ledger.note: 12 March 1948: the Union of Baghelkhand and Bundelkhand States, later Vindhya Pradesh, is formed from the eastern princely states of the Central India Agency. 'Vindhya Pradesh state was formed on 12 March 1948 and inaugurated on 4 April 1948'; '36 princely states were merged to form Vindhya Pradesh state' (Rewa, Panna, Datia, Orchha, Chhatarpur, Charkhari, Maihar, Nagod, Samthar named); capital Rewa. The page gives the states, not an outline: the region is the researcher's.

12 March 1948: Rewa merges into the new union. Rewa is the first of the 36 merged states on the page and its maharaja Martand Singh was Rajpramukh from 4 April 1948. The rewa-state dossier books the matching dissolve; the outline is that dossier's hand-drawn Baghelkhand plateau.

region.text: the Bundelkhand states and the small Baghelkhand states: Panna, Chhatarpur, Datia, Orchha, Maihar, Nagod, Samthar and the rest of the 36

ledger.counterpart: the other thirty-five princely states of the eastern Central India Agency (Panna, Datia, Orchha, Chhatarpur, Charkhari, Maihar, Nagod, Samthar named)
ledger.note: 12 March 1948: the Bundelkhand states join. 'In 1948, the eastern regions of Central India Agency became the Union of Baghelkhand and Bundelkhand States'; the Bundelkhand division had its headquarters at Nowgaon. These states have no dossier, so the counterpart is the page's description (the madhya-bharat ledger does the same for its states).

1 January 1950: the union becomes the Part C state of Vindhya Pradesh under a Chief Commissioner. 'It was renamed Vindhya Pradesh and converted to a Part C state, headed by a Chief Commissioner, on 1 January 1950'; the same page says 'It was named as Vindhya Pradesh on 25 January 1950 after the Vindhya Range'. The Rajpramukh (Martand Singh) held office until 31 December 1949. Charkhari and Samthar left on 25 January 1950 (outside the drawn region). Confidence 2 (n-mid review): the page gives two dates for the renaming, 1 January and 25 January 1950.

region.text: Vindhya Pradesh, 61,131.5 km2: the eastern princely states of the former Central India Agency, the Baghelkhand division (Rewa, Nagod, Maihar, and the rest of the plateau) and the Bundelkhand division (Panna, Chhatarpur, Orchha, Datia and the rest)

ledger.note: 1 November 1956: Vindhya Pradesh is merged into Madhya Pradesh. 'The state was dissolved on 31 October 1956 and merged with Madhya Pradesh'; 'merged into Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 1956' (the States Reorganisation of 1956). In 1952 it had become a Part A state under a Lieutenant Governor.

certainty.note: A state of the Indian Union with administrative boundaries (eight districts), but the page gives no outline: the drawn edge follows the Rewa outline and discs and is approximate; Charkhari and Samthar are left out.

sources.title: Vindhya Pradesh
sources.note: Formation 12 March 1948 (inaugurated 4 April 1948), the 36 states, 1 January / 25 January 1950 Part C status, 1952 Part A, 31 October / 1 November 1956 merger, capital Rewa, area 61,131.5 km2, rajpramukh and chief commissioners, divisions. No district names, no outline.

sources.title: Baghelkhand
sources.note: Extent of the Baghelkhand region (42,179 km2, Singrauli, Rewa, Satna, Shahdol, Sidhi, Anuppur, Umaria, Maihar, Mauganj) and the Baghelkhand Agency (Rewa and 11 minor states: Maihar, Nagod, Sohawal, Jaso, Kothi, Baraundha). Does not mention Vindhya Pradesh.

notes: Requested by the p1940-p1949 window (Rewa and the neighbouring Baghelkhand states are nobody's in the compiled map from 1948). The rewa-state dossier already lists this slug as its successor with the same hand-drawn outline; this dossier adds the Bundelkhand and the smaller Baghelkhand states as one union with the infobox's 61,131.5 km2. Not settled: the 36 states are not listed in the extracts read (the page names Rewa, Panna, Datia, Orchha, Chhatarpur, Charkhari, Maihar, Nagod and Samthar), no dossier exists for any except Rewa; the eight district names and the exact outline; the page's two dates for the naming and Part C status (1 January and 25 January 1950). Cliopatria has no rows for any of this land after Rewa's absence. Successors and predecessors named by slug need dossiers: madhya-pradesh (also named by madhya-bharat) and central-india-agency (the infobox predecessor). Gazetteer names needed: Baghelkhand (region), Chhatarpur, Panna (India), Datia, Orchha, Satna, Sidhi, Nowgaon (Nowgong), Charkhari. The region uses two coordinate discs (79.9 E 24.8 N, 140 km; 78.46 E 25.67 N, 45 km) as a stand-in for Panna-Chhatarpur-Tikamgarh and Datia-Orchha; those centres are the researcher's, not a page's.
